source_evidence.observation: The standing problem is Ax=b with square nonsingular A∈R^{n×n} and 0≠b∈R^n. Left and right preconditioners M_L and M_R are nonsingular.

The paper invokes the standard floating-point model of [23, sec. 2.2], writes fl(·) for a computed value, and allows u_m,u_a,u_g to denote either an arithmetic or its unit roundoff, assumed substantially below 1.

source_evidence.anchor: Section 2, c(n,k), approximate inequalities, norms, and equation (2.1)
source_evidence.observation: The paper calls c(n,k) generic low-degree polynomials in n and k whose precise values are not always tracked. It uses ≲ and ≈ when negligible second-order terms are dropped, defines ≫ qualitatively, defines singular values, 2- and Frobenius norms and several condition numbers, and defines forward error as ||xhat−x||_2/||x||_2.

Ztilde_k is an input search-space basis. Algorithm 2 computes C_k=M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k and btilde=M_L^{-1}b, solves min_y||btilde−C_ky||_2 using MGS, Givens rotations and a triangular solve, and forms x_k=Ztilde_ky_k. In exact arithmetic Ztilde_k may be taken as M_R^{-1}V_k, but in the error analysis it can differ from the computed basis Zhat_k.

source_evidence.anchor: equations (3.2)-(3.6) and the MGS/Givens least-squares statement
source_evidence.observation: The four operation guarantees are Chat_k=M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k+Δ_c with ||Δ_c||_F≤ε_c||M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k||_F; bhat=btilde+Δ_b with ||Δ_b||_2≤ε_b||btilde||_2; the stated MGS/Givens perturbed least-squares guarantee for yhat_k, conditional on u_gκ(Chat_k)≪1; and xhat_k=Ztilde_kyhat_k+Δ_x with ||Δ_x||_2≤ε_x||Ztilde_kyhat_k||_2. The additional conditions are (ε_c+ε_b+u_g)κ(M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k)≪1 and ε_x≪1.

For an increasing full-rank search-space basis there exists k≤n such that σ_min(Vhat_k)^{-1}≤4/3 and σ_max(Vhat_k)≤4/3. At that k, under (3.2)-(3.6), for every nonsingular M_R the theorem gives ||xhat_k−x||_2/||x||_2≲c(n,k)ξκ(M_L^{-1}AM_R^{-1}), with ξ=αε_c+βε_b+βu_g+λε_x and the displayed formulas for α,β,λ.

source_evidence.anchor: Appendix A, equation (A.1) and cited MGS dimension argument
source_evidence.observation: Appendix A recalls [11, eqs. (5.15)-(5.17)]: for any increasing nonsingular basis there is one k≤n which works for every φ>0 and, if k≤n−1, satisfies σ_min([M_L^{-1}b φ,M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k])<(c(n,k)u_g+ε_c)||[M_L^{-1}b φ,M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k]||_F, together with (3.7). The cited result originally has Ztilde_k≡Vhat_k and M_L≡I; this paper asserts that it adapts straightforwardly to the general case and takes that k for Theorem 3.1. It also imports ε_ls≡c(n,k)u_g and residual bounds (A.2)-(A.3) from [11], omitting the first two parts of that earlier proof.

After selecting k, the proof introduces an arbitrary nonsingular M_R and xhat_k^R=M_RZtilde_kyhat_k. It explicitly calls xhat_k^R a mathematical artifice, not an algorithm-level computed quantity, and locally constructs perturbations for the split-preconditioned system.

The proof uses ||xhat_k^R||_2≥σ_min(M_RZtilde_k)||yhat_k||_2, defines α''=σ_min(M_RZtilde_k)^{-1}||M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k||_F/||M_L^{-1}AM_R^{-1}||_F and β''=max(1,α''), and obtains split-system backward and forward bounds. It states that M_RZtilde_k is full rank because M_R is nonsingular and Ztilde_k is full rank.

Using (3.4), (1−ε_x)^{-1}, ||x_R||_2≤||M_R||_F||x||_2, and explicitly dropping second-order terms, the proof obtains ||xhat_k−x||_2/||x||_2≲c(n,k)ξ''κ(M_L^{-1}AM_R^{-1})κ(M_R)+ε_x and says this recovers (3.8).

binders: Fix the standing square nonsingular system A∈R^{n×n}, 0≠b∈R^n, with exact solution x, and a nonsingular left preconditioner M_L∈R^{n×n}. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, (1.1)-(1.2); PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, Theorem 3.1]
Fix Algorithm 2 applied along a full-rank search-space basis Ztilde_k∈R^{n×k} whose dimension increases with k≤n. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, Theorem 3.1]

For the fixed increasing search-space/computation sequence, there exists a selected dimension k≤n; after that selection, the bound is asserted for every nonsingular M_R∈R^{n×n}. Thus the selected k is independent of the later analytically quantified M_R, although it can depend on the fixed search-space sequence and its computed MGS process. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, Theorem 3.1; PDF p. 36, printed p. 35, (A.1); PDF p. 37, printed p. 36, (A.4)]

At the selected k, ε_c, ε_b and ε_x are the parameters of the line-1, line-2 and line-4 modular error bounds, and u_g is the unit roundoff used for the MGS/Givens GMRES operations. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, (3.2)-(3.6)]
The dimension-selection ingredient binds one k that satisfies its near-dependence condition for all real φ>0; the near-dependence clause is required only when k≤n−1. [PDF p. 36, printed p. 35, (A.1)]
hypotheses: The standing system has nonsingular A and nonzero b, and M_L is nonsingular. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, (1.1)-(1.2); PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, Theorem 3.1]
The search-space bases are full rank as their dimension increases up to n; this is an exact-rank hypothesis distinct from numerical nonsingularity of Chat_k. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, Theorem 3.1]

At the selected k, the matrix-product, right-hand-side, MGS/Givens least-squares, and solution-product guarantees associated with Algorithm 2 hold. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, (3.2)-(3.4) and the intervening least-squares statement]
The MGS/Givens least-squares guarantee additionally requires u_gκ(Chat_k)≪1. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, MGS/Givens least-squares statement]

At the selected k, (ε_c+ε_b+u_g)κ(M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k)≪1 and ε_x≪1. The current (3.6) is only ε_x≪1; it is not the older explicit numerical-rank condition on Ztilde_k discussed immediately afterward. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, (3.5)-(3.6)]
conclusions: There exists k≤n such that the computed Krylov basis satisfies both σ_min(Vhat_k)^{-1}≤4/3 and σ_max(Vhat_k)≤4/3, equivalently σ_min(Vhat_k)≥3/4 and σ_max(Vhat_k)≤4/3. Neither inequality may be dropped or replaced solely by a condition-number bound. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, (3.7)]
For that same k, if (3.2)-(3.6) hold, then for every nonsingular M_R, ||xhat_k−x||_2/||x||_2≲c(n,k)ξκ(M_L^{-1}AM_R^{-1}). [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, (3.8)]
The theorem is existential in the iteration/dimension k; it does not assert the bound for every k or an entire convergence history. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, Theorem 3.1]
definitions_and_conventions: Let S=M_L^{-1}AM_R^{-1}. Then α=[κ(M_R)/σ_min(M_RZtilde_k)]·[||M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k||_F/||S||_F]. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, definition of α following (3.8)]

β=max{1,[||M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k||_F/||S||_F]/σ_min(M_RZtilde_k)}·κ(M_R), with κ(M_R) outside the maximum. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, definition of β following (3.8); PDF pp. 38-39, printed pp. 37-38, α'', β'' and (A.11)]
λ=1/κ(S), and ξ=αε_c+βε_b+βu_g+λε_x. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, (3.8)]

Appendix A uses α''=[||M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k||_F/||S||_F]/σ_min(M_RZtilde_k), β''=max(1,α''), and ξ''=α''ε_c+β''ε_b+β''u_g; hence α=κ(M_R)α'', β=κ(M_R)β'', and λ=κ(S)^{-1}. [PDF p. 38, printed p. 37, (A.9); PDF p. 39, printed p. 38, (A.11); PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, (3.8)]

The symbol c(n,k) denotes generic polynomial factors in n and k of qualitatively low degree; the paper does not always track their precise values. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2; PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, after (3.8)]

The notation ≡ means that a quantity under the analyst's control and not fixed may be taken equal to the displayed quantity; it is not introduced as logical equivalence. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2]
The proof quantity xhat_k^R=M_RZtilde_kyhat_k is linked to the computed yhat_k but is expressly a mathematical artifice, not an actual computed algorithm variable. [PDF p. 37, printed p. 36, (A.4)]
implicit_context: Provenance supplied by the source locator: source_locator_sha256=75e3f221aaf71e9ad2abdab996037f606bf419f70ab7492dc0d49679d3309820; this is locator metadata, not a mathematical claim from the PDF.

Algorithm 2 takes Ztilde_k directly as input. In exact arithmetic it may be chosen as M_R^{-1}V_k, while in finite precision it may deliberately differ from the naturally computed Zhat_k to absorb rounding errors. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, discussion before Algorithm 2]

The M_R quantified after selecting k functions in Appendix A as an analytical split-preconditioning matrix; Algorithm 2 has no separate M_R operation once Ztilde_k is fixed. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, Algorithm 2; PDF p. 37, printed p. 36, (A.4)]

The existence and conditioning of the selected k are not proved from scratch here: they are recalled from [11, eqs. (5.15)-(5.17)], and the extension from Ztilde_k≡Vhat_k, M_L≡I to general Ztilde_k and M_L is asserted to be straightforward. [PDF p. 36, printed p. 35, discussion of (A.1)]

The fixed MGS least-squares accuracy ε_ls≡c(n,k)u_g and residual relations (A.2)-(A.3) are imported from [11]; the paper says the first two parts of the prior proof are not presented. The split-system perturbation and forward-error propagation from (A.4) through (A.11) are developed locally. [PDF pp. 36-39, printed pp. 35-38, Appendix A]
statement.algorithm_linkage: Algorithm 2 has four operations: (1) C_k=M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k; (2) btilde=M_L^{-1}b; (3) solve min_y||btilde−C_ky||_2 by MGS with [btilde,C_k]=[V_k,v_{k+1}][β_alg e_1,Hbar_k], followed by Givens rotations and a triangular solve; and (4) x_k=Ztilde_ky_k. The computed basis Vhat_{k+1} comes from applying MGS to [bhat,Chat_k], while (3.7) concerns Vhat_k. The QR scalar β_alg=||btilde||_2 is distinct from the coefficient β defined in Theorem 3.1. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, (3.1) and Algorithm 2; PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, least-squares discussion; PDF p. 36, printed p. 35, (A.1)]
numerical_model: The analysis uses a cited standard floating-point model, with fl(·) denoting a computed value and u_g the GMRES-operation unit roundoff. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 4, Section 2; PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, least-squares model]
Line 2: bhat=fl(M_L^{-1}b)=btilde+Δ_b and ||Δ_b||_2≤ε_b||btilde||_2, where btilde=M_L^{-1}b. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, (3.3)]

Line 3: yhat_k=argmin_y||bhat+Δ_b^{ls}−(Chat_k+Δ_c^{ls})y||_2 and, for every j≤k+1, ||[Δ_b^{ls},Δ_c^{ls}]e_j||_2≤c(n,k)u_g||[bhat,Chat_k]e_j||_2, provided u_gκ(Chat_k)≪1. This is a cited MGS/Givens accuracy result rather than a free ε_ls model. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, unnumbered least-squares guarantee; PDF p. 36, printed p. 35, ε_ls discussion]
The remaining selected-k conditions are (ε_c+ε_b+u_g)κ(M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k)≪1 and ε_x≪1. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, (3.5)-(3.6)]
error_notions: The conclusion concerns normalized normwise forward error ||xhat_k−x||_2/||x||_2 for the original system Ax=b. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, (2.1); PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, (3.8)]

Appendix A first derives a normwise backward error for the analytically split system, converts it to split-system forward error, and then returns to the original-system forward error. These are proof intermediates, not additional universal conclusions of Theorem 3.1. [PDF pp. 38-39, printed pp. 37-38, (A.8)-(A.11)]

The word attainable refers to the error reached at the existentially selected dimension k, not an exact solution guarantee or a bound at every iteration. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, text before and within Theorem 3.1]
norms: Vector ||·||_2 is Euclidean; matrix ||·||_2 is the induced 2-norm; ||·||_F is the Frobenius norm; σ_min and σ_max are defined for rectangular matrices. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2]

For square nonsingular B, the paper defines κ_F(B)=||B^{-1}||_F||B||_F, κ_2(B)=σ_max(B)/σ_min(B), and κ_{F,2}=||B||_F/σ_min(B), then writes κ(B) when it does not distinguish these equivalent normwise quantities. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2]

The formulas for α and β use Frobenius norms explicitly and the smallest singular value of the rectangular matrix M_RZtilde_k; the outer condition numbers are written generically as κ. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, formulas following (3.8)]

Full column rank of Ztilde_k and nonsingularity of M_R imply σ_min(M_RZtilde_k)>0. Nonsingularity of A,M_L,M_R makes S=M_L^{-1}AM_R^{-1} nonsingular. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, (1.1)-(1.2); PDF p. 38, printed p. 37, paragraph following (A.9)]
constants_and_indexing: The selected iteration satisfies k≤n. If k≤n−1, (A.1) adds the near-dependence inequality; when k=n that clause is not required, while (3.7) still is. [PDF p. 36, printed p. 35, (A.1)]
The same selected k must make (A.1) hold for every φ>0, not merely for one φ chosen after k. [PDF p. 36, printed p. 35, (A.1)]

In the least-squares perturbation guarantee, j≤k+1 indexes the columns of the concatenated n×(k+1) matrices [bhat,Chat_k] and [Δ_b^{ls},Δ_c^{ls}] via e_j. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, least-squares guarantee]
The symbol β is overloaded: β_alg=||btilde||_2 in the Arnoldi/QR relation, whereas Theorem 3.1's β is max(1,α'')κ(M_R). [PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, (3.1); PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, (3.8)]

The source guarantees only that each generic c(n,k) is a polynomial in n and k of low degree; it supplies no numerical degree bound, coefficient list, coefficient-sign restriction, normalization, or statement that all occurrences denote one fixed polynomial. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2]
higher_order_terms: The source defines ≲ and ≈ as notation used when negligible second-order terms are dropped. It does not define ≲ as an exact order relation or ordinary ≤. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2]

The paper states no limiting variable, asymptotic filter, quantified threshold, hidden-constant bound, or explicit list of terms that makes 'negligible second order' formal. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, notation paragraph; PDF p. 39, printed p. 38, derivation of (A.11)]

The symbols ≪ and ≫ are qualitative: Θ_1≫Θ_2 means 'much greater', with the convention that Θ_1≫Θ_2 permits Θ_1≫c(n,k)Θ_2. No numeric cutoff is supplied for (3.5), (3.6), or u_gκ(Chat_k)≪1. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, notation paragraph; PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, smallness conditions]

Equation (A.11), and therefore (3.8), is explicitly first-order: the proof uses (1−ε_x)^{-1}, absorbs terms, and says it drops second-order terms before recovering the theorem. [PDF p. 39, printed p. 38, (A.11)]
exceptional_values: The cited standard floating-point model and the real-valued perturbation equations are the only stated computational framework. The theorem passage does not explicitly discuss NaNs, infinities, overflow, underflow, subnormals, or how an exceptional result would satisfy the models. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 4, floating-point-model paragraph; PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, (3.2)-(3.4)]

The standing assumptions A nonsingular and b≠0 imply x=A^{-1}b≠0, so the forward-error denominator ||x||_2 is positive. Full rank and nonsingularity make the displayed denominators in α,β,λ positive and finite under ordinary real arithmetic. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, (1.1)-(1.2); PDF p. 38, printed p. 37, paragraph after (A.9)]

The least-squares model explicitly excludes numerical singularity through u_gκ(Chat_k)≪1, but the paper gives no separate breakdown or exceptional-value branch. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, least-squares guarantee]

Appendix A divides by ||xhat_k^R||_2 and ||xhat_k^R||_2^2 when constructing perturbations, but it does not explicitly assume or prove yhat_k≠0 or xhat_k^R≠0 at that point. Its later full-rank observation ensures xhat_k^R≠0 only if yhat_k≠0. [PDF p. 37, printed p. 36, (A.4)-(A.7); PDF p. 38, printed p. 37, paragraph after (A.9)]

undebatable_constraints: The quantifier order is: fix the increasing full-rank search-space/computation sequence and M_L; select one k≤n; at that k require the modular hypotheses; then the error bound holds for every nonsingular analytical M_R. The selected k is not allowed to depend on that later M_R. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, Theorem 3.1; PDF pp. 36-37, printed pp. 35-36, (A.1) and (A.4)]
Equation (3.7) requires separately σ_min(Vhat_k)^{-1}≤4/3 and σ_max(Vhat_k)≤4/3 for the computed Krylov basis. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, (3.7)]

The increasing search-space basis is required to be full rank, while Chat_k must additionally satisfy its own numerical-nonsingularity condition for the MGS/Givens least-squares result. [PDF pp. 8-9, printed pp. 7-8, least-squares guarantee and Theorem 3.1]
At the selected k, all four Algorithm 2 operation guarantees and the smallness conditions (3.5)-(3.6) belong to the source contract. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, (3.2)-(3.6)]

The exact coefficient formulas are α=κ(M_R)α'', β=κ(M_R)max(1,α''), λ=κ(M_L^{-1}AM_R^{-1})^{-1}, with α''=[||M_L^{-1}AZtilde_k||_F/||M_L^{-1}AM_R^{-1}||_F]/σ_min(M_RZtilde_k), and ξ=αε_c+βε_b+βu_g+λε_x. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, (3.8); PDF pp. 38-39, printed pp. 37-38, (A.9)-(A.11)]

The relation in (3.8) is a first-order ≲ statement with omitted negligible second-order terms, not an exact inequality, asymptotic theorem with a stated filter, or limit statement. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, notation paragraph; PDF p. 39, printed p. 38, (A.11)]

c(n,k) cannot faithfully be described as an arbitrary unrestricted scalar: the source calls it a generic low-degree polynomial in n and k, while leaving degree and coefficients unspecified. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2]

The theorem is nonvacuous for the normalized exact-solution error because A is nonsingular and b is nonzero; exceptional floating-point values are not explicitly modeled. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, (1.1); PDF p. 5, printed p. 4, floating-point-model paragraph]

contract_plain_english: For a fixed nonsingular system Ax=b with b≠0, a nonsingular left preconditioner, and a growing sequence of full-rank Algorithm 2 search-space bases, the paper selects one dimension k≤n using a cited MGS first-loss argument. The same k works for every φ>0 in (A.1), with the near-dependence clause needed only when k<n, and it satisfies both singular-value bounds in (3.7). At that selected k, the line-1, line-2, fixed MGS/Givens least-squares, and line-4 error guarantees and all three qualitative smallness requirements must hold. Only then, and after k has been selected, every nonsingular analytical M_R gives the first-order forward-error estimate (3.8) with the exact α, β, λ and ξ formulas above. The selected k does not depend on this later M_R. The dimension-selection, MGS least-squares accuracy, and initial residual propagation are imported or asserted adaptations of [11]; Appendix A locally develops the split-system propagation through (A.11). The symbols ≲, ≪ and c(n,k) remain informal in mathematically material ways: no exact remainder, limiting filter, numerical threshold, polynomial degree, or coefficients are supplied. Ordinary nonvacuity follows from nonsingularity, b≠0 and full rank, but exceptional floating-point values and the possible zero denominator xhat_k^R are not explicitly resolved. [PDF pp. 3, 6-9, and 36-39, printed pp. 2, 5-8, and 35-38, equations (1.1), (2.1), (3.2)-(3.8), and (A.1)-(A.11)]
